transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-06-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Ortega (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Sofia Martins (Hearthline CTO); Ethan Cole (Lead Backend); Maya Robinson (Security); Noah Patel (Product)

Auto-summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on chat gen basics. Demoed streaming and how to tune generation params for low latency. Discussed retry/backoff strategies and enterprise security requirements (SOC2, KMS). Agreed next steps: sandbox access + benchmarks.

[00:00] Liam Ortega: Hey all, thanks for joining. I'm Liam, AE on Redwood Inference, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Sofia Martins: Hi Liam, doing well. Busy week but excited — we're looking at adding conversational summaries to our care coordinator workflow.
[00:14] Liam Ortega: Awesome. Priya will walk through the hosted chat quickstart, streaming behavior, and then we'll cover retries and a suggested rescue plan. We can pause for questions any time.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Hi team. Quick agenda: 1) brief API orientation, 2) live sandbox run (small prompt set), 3) talk params that affect latency and cost, 4) retry/rescue patterns, 5) security notes.
[00:34] Ethan Cole: Sounds good. Quick note: our infra is in GCP, we prefer VPC peering for dedicated later, but for sandbox hosted is fine. Also we need to keep PHI out of logging by default.
[00:45] Priya Nair: Got it — we'll show you how to configure logging/data retention and KMS.

--- Live demo segment ---
[01:10] Priya Nair: Ok I'm switched into the console, but I'll do one curl call to the hosted API so you can see streaming in the terminal. First call is a short patient-note summarization prompt.
[01:28] Priya Nair: (typing) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chatgen -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize: Patient reported mild chest pain..."}], "stream": true, "max_tokens": 120, "temperature": 0.2}'
[01:45] [Transcript artifact: stream chunks arriving]
[01:50] Sofia Martins: I like how partial tokens come quickly, that's key for our clinician UI — want to render progressive text.
[01:56] Priya Nair: Exactly. Streaming sends chunks as they're decoded. Note there's tradeoff if you enable larger decode buffers — you'll get slightly higher throughput but chunk latency increases.
[02:10] Ethan Cole: Can we control chunk size?
[02:13] Priya Nair: You can tune server-side decode batch sizes via console Optimize suggestions, and client-side you can adjust how you buffer the stream. We expose a parameter called "stream_chunk_hint" in the SDK — it's a soft hint.
[02:26] Maya Robinson: Is that field officially supported? We need it documented for audit.
[02:30] Priya Nair: Yeah it's in the docs; I think earlier auto transcriptions sometimes show it as "stream chunk..." or mis-typed but it's a supported tuning knob. We'll send the doc link after.

[02:50] Priya Nair: Next, params that control latency/cost. max_tokens, temperature, top_p, and presence penalties. Also shorter prompts obviously reduce per-request cost.
[03:05] Liam Ortega: For Hearthline, given you care about latency for clinicians, we'd recommend low temperature (0.0-0.3), shorter max_tokens for inline responses, and using prefix caching for repeated templates.
[03:20] Sofia Martins: Can you explain prefix caching again?
[03:23] Priya Nair: Sure. If you have a large shared prompt prefix — like system instructions or patient context — Redwood will KV cache the key-value states so subsequent calls only send deltas. It reduces compute and latency. Sometimes our ASR shows "K V cash" but it's actually KV cache.
[03:40] Ethan Cole: That helps. Does prefix cache interact poorly with patient-specific PHI?
[03:45] Priya Nair: Good point — you can configure what is cached and what is ephemeral. For PHI we typically recommend not caching the raw PHI; instead cache embeddings or anonymized context. Also we have tenant-level retention controls.

[04:05] Priya Nair: Ok demo 2: show a case where the stream stalls and how client should implement retries.
[04:12] (demo) Priya triggers a controlled rate-limited response and the stream sends an error mid-response.
[04:22] [Demo noise: audible keyboard, brief pause]
[04:30] Priya Nair: So the stream returned a partial and then an error code 503 and a message "service overloaded". Best practice: capture the last stable token, retry with the same conversation id and set an idempotency token so the server can resume or provide a deterministic fallback.
[04:50] Ethan Cole: Wait is conversation_id required for resume?
[04:53] Priya Nair: Not required but recommended. For guaranteed resume behavior you should pass conversation_id + client_resume_token. On hosted we support automatic resume for short-lived KV states; for long resumptions, it's better to persist KV externally.
[05:10] Sofia Martins: How about backoff strategy? Exponential? Jitter?
[05:14] Priya Nair: Exponential backoff with jitter is our standard. Start at 300ms, double up to a ceiling like 8s. For user-facing flows you can show a tiny spinner and prefetch a conservative fallback answer from the cache.
[05:26] Liam Ortega: And for critical flows where a slight stale answer is better than nothing, configure fallback model variants — e.g., route to a smaller, cheaper quantized variant that has slightly different quality but stays online.
[05:40] Maya Robinson: That implies we'd accept lower-quality output during outages. We need to document when that happens for clinicians.
[05:46] Priya Nair: Absolutely — we have hooks that emit an event when fallback routing occurs; those events go to audit logs. We'll show the console settings.

[06:10] Priya Nair: Quick tour of the console: here is per-route latency breakdown, token cost graphs, and a toggle to enable canary fallback models. You can also pin config per-route.
[06:25] (screen share) "Console: Route detail -> latency histogram"
[06:40] Ethan Cole: On the latency histogram, what percentiles should we watch for clinical SLAs?
[06:45] Priya Nair: For interactive clinician UIs we recommend P95 < 500ms for short responses, P99 < 1.5s. But depends on your exact prompt sizes. Optimize will suggest batching and quantization profiles to meet these.

[07:10] Sofia Martins: Our concern: PHI never leaves region, we need data residency and KMS. How does hosted handle customer-managed keys?
[07:18] Priya Nair: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments and for hosted we can integrate with cloud KMS via per-tenant encryption. We'll attach the architecture doc. For strict air-gapped PHI flows we recommend Redwood Private.
[07:33] Maya Robinson: SOC2 is non-negotiable — can you send SOC2 Type II report?
[07:37] Liam Ortega: Yes, Priya will attach SOC2 and our penetration test summary.

[07:50] --- Questions and edge cases ---
[08:00] Ethan Cole: If we do a short POC, what's the recommended load testing cadence?
[08:05] Priya Nair: Start small: 1 TPS with your canonical prompt flows for 24h, then scale to target TPS in a staged way. We'll run a benchmark with you; Redwood Dedicated later gives predictable throughput.
[08:18] Noah Patel: For the sandbox, do we get a dedicated environment or multi-tenant hosted?
[08:22] Liam Ortega: Sandbox is multi-tenant hosted, isolated by tenant id and with no persisted PII by default. If you need VPC peering or dedicated GPUs, move to Dedicated or Private.

[08:40] Sofia Martins: Can we set token-level redaction? E.g., redact PHI from logs automatically?
[08:44] Priya Nair: Yes, you can enable token redaction pipeline. That hooks into our retention policy and prevents conversation text from being written to logs. We'll send the doc link.

[09:05] Priya Nair: Last demo: show how Optimize suggests configurations. I uploaded a sample workload (the prompt set Ethan sent earlier). Optimize recommends: enable prefix caching for repeated templates, lower decode buffer for better chunk latency, and switch to int8 quantized variant for cost savings if throughput is high.
[09:25] Ethan Cole: Quantized variant — do we lose accuracy?
[09:28] Priya Nair: Slight delta in some edge cases; Optimize includes A/B check to validate output quality on your eval set before switching. We'll run that as part of the benchmark.

[09:45] (short silence)
[09:52] Priya Nair: Ok that's most of the demo — let's surface a rescue plan in bullet points.
[10:00] Liam Ortega: Rescue plan: 1) instrument streaming with client resume + idempotency tokens, 2) implement exponential backoff with jitter and spinner UI, 3) enable prefix cache for templates, 4) configure fallback model variant and audit hook for fallbacks, 5) set retention/redaction for PHI in logs.
[10:20] Sofia Martins: Good. For step 1, can Redwood help instrument the client?
[10:25] Priya Nair: Yes, we have an SDK snippet and a sample middleware that shows resume and token sync; we'll push code to the sandbox repo.

--- Closing / Recap ---
[10:40] Liam Ortega: Quick recap: we will provide sandbox creds by tomorrow, Priya will attach compliance docs, and we'll run a 24h benchmark with your prompts. After results, we'll do POC scoping call 7/7 to decide Dedicated vs Hosted+VPC.
[10:58] Sofia Martins: That timeline works. Thank you both — this was very practical.
[11:04] Maya Robinson: Please include the exact retention config options in the email.
[11:08] Priya Nair: Will do, Maya.
[11:12] Ethan Cole: I'll drop the canonical prompts and expected TPS into the shared folder after the call.
[11:16] Liam Ortega: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and next steps.
[11:20] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional filler words removed for readability but some mis-hearings kept (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache, "stream chunk hint" variations).

End of transcript.
